decisive_items: Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL (normal 4.8–105)
diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk
response.rationale: The vignette explicitly links hypopituitarism, elevated IgG4, pituitary/stalk swelling, and systemic findings (lung nodule, sinus thickening) to IgG4-related disease. R1 directly matches these features. R3 (lymphocytic hypophysitis) shares pituitary swelling and hypopituitarism but lacks the IgG4 elevation and systemic involvement, making it a secondary differential. R2 and R4 are less supported by the overall pattern.

rejected.why: Sinus and lung findings are nonspecific; no IgG4 elevation or pituitary stalk involvement characteristic of GPA.
Elevated IgG4 and systemic IgG4-related disease point away from isolated lymphocytic hypophysitis.
The 7-mm mass is a minor finding; clinical and laboratory context strongly favor an inflammatory process, not lymphoma.
